content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper is based on ConvSA. It claims that the limitation of ConvSA is that the dynamic kernel is reduced to the identical pattern with scale-based weighting. It tries to modify this ConvSA by considering D-dimensional vectors (instead of using scales). It can be estimated that using a high-dimensional vector is better than using a scale for encoding structural correlations (in attention or feature maps). However, this novelty is incremental compared to the existing work ConvSA.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

This paper aims to improve visual transformers by considering encoding structural correlations. It is an interesting research problem. In addition, the proposed method is validated widely on popular benchmarks, and shown to achieve consistent performance improvements over related methods.

Weakness:

The proposed approach is a bit incremental compared to its baseline method ConvSA. It simply converts a weighing scale from one dimension to multiple dimensions (from a scale to a vector). 

The performance of the proposed method is consistently improved over related methods. However, the margins are quite limited to less than (or equal to) 0.5% on the most standard benchmark ImageNet-1K.

The writing of this paper is poor, especially in the section of Introduction. It mixes a lot of keywords such as structure, correlation, attention and variant without introducing or giving any intuitive description of them. It is a bit tough for readers to follow the Introduction without checking the details in the section of the method.

Weakness: The innovation is not enough.Only the pattern detector uK and the context aggregator uV are extended  to matrices UK,UV. The structure of the network doesn't change much as in Uniformer (Li et al., 2022a). The improvement is limited.

content.title: StructViT: Learning Correlation Structures for Vision Transformers
content.TL;DR: We introduce structural self-attention (StructSA) that exploits geometric structures of query-key correlations and the proposed network StructViT achieves state-of-the-art results on various image and video classification benchmarks.
content.abstract: We introduce the structural self-attention (StructSA) mechanism that leverages structural patterns of query-key correlation for visual representation learning. StructSA generates attention by recognizing space-time structures of correlations and performs long-range interactions across entire locations, effectively capturing structural patterns, e.g., spatial layouts, motion, or inter-object relations in images and videos. Using StructSA as a main building block, we develop the structural vision transformer (StructViT) and evaluate its effectiveness on both image and video classification tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on ImageNet-1K, Kinetics-400, Something-Something V1 & V2, Diving-48, and FineGym.
